overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to send its response to a prior complaint within 14 business days, but not intentionally. The executive session procedure allegations were not violations.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly adjourned into executive session without taking the required procedural steps, including the chair's announcement about reconvening.
allegations.key_passage: Because the method of “adequate, alternative” access to the Board’s January 18 meeting, as clearly stated on the meeting notice, was Zoom, the fact that the DCTV recording ended before the announcement was made does not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to respond to a prior Open Meeting Law complaint within the 14 business days allowed by law.
allegations.key_passage: As the response was sent more than 14 business days after receipt of the complaint, the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the late response to the prior complaint was an intentional violation of the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the violation was not intentional.

allegations.summary: Complainant objected that the Board listed an executive session to deliberate on and respond to Open Meeting Law complaints.
allegations.key_passage: our office has unequivocally stated in numerous past determinations that public bodies may meet in executive session under Purpose 1 to review Open Meeting Law complaints against the body or its members.
